children: South Korea’s Hanwha Engineering & Construction (Hanwha E&C) plans to withdraw from Iraq’s nearly $10 billion Bismayah residential development and terminate its Iraqi workforce, citing prolonged delays in payments by the National Investment Commission (NIC), according to a report from local Arabic language newspaper Shafaq News.
Located about 10 kilometres south of Baghdad, the integrated development spans 18.3 square kilometres (sq km) and is designed to comprise 100,000 housing units.
According to the report, Hanwha’s letter to the NIC highlighted “serious administrative and financial difficulties” faced by the company because of delays in receiving payments for completed work.

The company said it had continued to bear employee salaries and general administrative expenses since March 2020 despite delays in project approvals and the payment of $270 million in outstanding dues for completed work.
Hanwha said the NIC had pledged over the past seven years to settle the outstanding amount but had yet to make the payments, leaving it unable to continue maintaining its Iraqi workforce.
The company notified the commission that its employment relationship with the employees would end on 16 October 2026, making 15 October their final working day.
The planned withdrawal has raised concerns among residents over the continuity of essential services at Bismayah, including drinking water supplies, Shafaq News reported.
Hanwha E&C was awarded the Bismayah project by the NIC in May 2012.
The latest development follows an earlier attempt by Hanwha to exit the project over unpaid dues.

In October 2022, South Korea-based English language business news portal KED Global reported that Hanwha had terminated its involvement in the project after years of payment delays by the Iraqi government. At the time, the company faced potential losses of up to 828 billion South Korean won ($581 million) if it failed to recover outstanding payments.
(Writing by Majda Muhsen; Editing by Anoop Menon)

title: South Korea’s Hanwha to withdraw from Iraq’s $10bln Bismayah housing project
